name: convert_depth_batch
doc:
Batch convert raw depth data to display-ready format.

Accepts raw order book entries (bids + asks) along with instrument context
and returns formatted depth items with:
- Price rounded to ladder precision (bid DOWN, ask UP)
- Amount converted per user's trade unit preference
- Cumulative sum amounts and bar fill ratios

# Arguments
* `request` - Contains instrument info, raw depth entries, display size,
ladder precision, and trade unit preference.

# Returns
`OKTDepthConvertResult` with formatted bid and ask lists.

# Conversion Pipeline
1. Slice bids/asks to `depth_size`
2. For each entry:
a. Parse origin price and amount
b. Convert quantity per trade unit (contract/coin/U)
c. Pass raw price + amount as strings (Decimal.to_string())
d. Pass precision metadata: `ladder_digits`, `amount_digit`, `is_bid`
e. Handle special case: price=0, amount!=0 → display "<ladder"
3. Compute cumulative sum_amount per side
4. Compute ratio = sum_amount / max_sum_amount

# Formatting Note
Prices and amounts are returned as RAW numeric strings without any
formatting (no rounding, no locale separators, no K/M/B/T suffixes).
The Kotlin/Swift UI layer applies all formatting using the metadata
fields (`ladder_digits`, `amount_digit`, `is_bid`) via `OKTNumberF`.

fields.doc:
Sign display mode: 0=AUTO, 1=ALWAYS, 2=EXCEPT_ZERO

The sign POLICY is a business decision and therefore belongs to the producer,
not to the renderer: a balance/valuation/price must never show a leading `+`
while a PnL must (Native `formatDexAssetBalanceUsd` -> `¥6.66` vs
`formatDexAssetPnl` -> `+¥6.66`, both through the same
`formatUsdValueToLocalValue`, differing only in `signType`).

Before this field existed both Kotlin resolvers hardcoded EXCEPT_ZERO, so every
producer got a `+` (device 2026-09-23: the DEX row valuation rendered `+¥17.32`
where Native shows `¥17.32`). Same shape as [`DisplayString::Percent`] and
[`DisplayString::Pnl`], which already carry this field.

Native cannot be handed a pre-signed string instead: the resolver parses the
value through `toSafeDouble()` before `formatFiatSymbol`, which drops a `+`.

variants.doc:
Fiat currency value that requires full ICU formatting on the native side.

Used exclusively for PnL values that have been converted from USD to the
user's selected local fiat currency. Rust provides the already-converted
numeric value; native formats it with ICU `formatFiatSymbol` which handles:
- Correct sign position (e.g., "-$1,134.64" not "$-1,134.64")
- RTL language support (Arabic, Hebrew)
- Locale-specific thousands separator and decimal point

# Fields
- `value`: Already-converted fiat value as string, e.g. "-1134.77" (no thousands sep)
- `iso_code`: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. "USD", "CNY", "EUR"

# Native usage (Kotlin)
```kotlin
value.toSafeDouble().formatFiatSymbol(
code = isoCode,
roundingMode = RoundingMode.HALF_DOWN,
signType = DisplaySign.EXCEPT_ZERO
)
```

variants.doc:
DEX token price formatted in local fiat currency with subscript-style notation.

Used exclusively for DEX asset price fields (average buy price, last price).
Rust provides the USD→local-fiat converted raw value; native formats it with
`formatFiatSymbolWithSubscriptStyle` which renders leading zeros as Unicode
subscript characters (e.g. "$0.₀₀₀₀₅" for 0.000050 USD).

# Fields
- `value`: Already fiat-converted raw numeric string, e.g. "0.000365" for CNY price
- `iso_code`: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. "USD", "CNY"

# Native usage (Kotlin)
Kotlin recomputes `Precision` from the value's magnitude (matching `formatDexPrice` rules):
- `== 0`         → `fixedPrecision(2)`
- `< 1`          → `significantPrecision(1, 5)`
- `[1, 10)`      → `minMaxPrecision(0, 4)`
- `[10, 1000)`   → `maxPrecision(OKTDexCurrencyAmountFormat.getCurrentIosBean().precision)`
Then calls `value.toSafeBigDecimal().formatFiatSymbolWithSubscriptStyle(code, DOWN, precision)`.

variants.name: TradingNumber

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Truncated / trailing-zeros-aligned plain decimal string (Rust-native sign).

fields.name: sign
fields.doc: Literal currency sign for prefix path (`"$"` / `"¥"`); mutually exclusive with `symbol`.

fields.name: symbol
fields.doc: Literal unit for suffix path (`"USDT"` / `"BTC"`); mutually exclusive with `sign`.

fields.name: polarity
fields.doc: Sign polarity strategy; defaults to `Auto`.

variants.doc:
V2 generic trading-numeric variant — covers price / amount / PnL /
available balance / max-buy / available margin / any trading metric that
needs locale thousand separators + literal sign/symbol + sign polarity.

Rust already handles truncation / trailing zeros / unit conversion; native
only adds the locale thousand separators, literal sign/symbol concatenation,
and the `+` prefix when polarity asks for it. Rendering MUST go through one
of three native entry points:
- `String.formatRustNumber(polarity)`  — value only
- `String.formatWithPrefix(sign, polarity)`  — sign prefix
- `String.formatWithSuffix(symbol, polarity)` — symbol suffix

# Field contract
- `value`: truncated / trailing-zeros-aligned plain decimal string. Negative
sign is Rust-native (`-12.50`); empty / placeholder cases must emit
`DisplayString::Placeholder` instead — `value` is never empty inside a
`TradingNumber`.
- `sign`: literal currency sign for prefix (`"$"` / `"¥"` / `"€"`).
- `symbol`: literal unit for suffix (`"USDT"` / `"BTC"` / `"USDC"`).
- `sign` and `symbol` are mutually exclusive — a value never carries both
`$` prefix AND ` USDT` suffix.
- `polarity`: controls whether positive values get a `+` prefix. Defaults
to `Polarity::Auto`.

# Out of scope (use V1 variants)
- DEX micro prices (subscript `0` shorthand) → `DisplayString::DexPrice`
- Percentages (24h change / yields) → `DisplayString::Percent` (ICU
`formatICUPercent`)
- Dates → `DisplayString::Date`
- CD keys → `DisplayString::CDKey` / `FormattedCDKey`

# Examples

```ignore
// Price "67,890.50 USDT"
DisplayString::TradingNumber {
value: "67890.50".to_string(),
sign: None,
symbol: Some("USDT".to_string()),
polarity: Polarity::Auto,
}

// Position PnL "+28.39 USDT"
DisplayString::TradingNumber {
value: "28.39".to_string(),
sign: None,
symbol: Some("USDT".to_string()),
polarity: Polarity::ExceptZero,
}

// Fiat balance "$500.00"
DisplayString::TradingNumber {
value: "500.00".to_string(),
sign: Some("$".to_string()),
symbol: None,
polarity: Polarity::Auto,
}
```

background load that decorates the interactor's OWN held
`PureTradeShareState::presentation` (the `prepare_position` /
`handleEvent` flow) — there, if a NEWER attempt lands and replaces
`state.presentation` before this load finishes, the stale result must
be dropped. A caller-supplied, self-contained presentation (history

has nothing for that revision to protect; checking it anyway means

four staleness guards (`background_revision` / `account_epoch` /
`watcher_generation` / manager request-current) keep doing their job.

That module is outside this workspace — see `cross_module_handoff_report.md`

carry the value across the FFI boundary.

source-compatible, exactly as for `display_symbol` above — required here
because the native cohort is frozen for this feature and must keep
compiling untouched.

state update feeds `calculate::recompute_price_currency_bubble`, which
drives the `≈ ¥XXXX (CNY)` / `≈ $XXXX (USD)` bubble below the price field.

Android until it migrates off the native-push round-trip.

`CurrencyRateManager` (`populate_fiat_rate_from_rust`, driven by

push them in. Android currently still reads
`getTradeDataSettings().getCurrentCurrencyData()` + `getLocalRate(...)`
out of Rust and pushes them back via this entry (a round-trip) — once
Android drops that hop this method can be removed. Until then it remains
a legal secondary writer of the SAME `state.usd_to_local_rate` /
`local_fiat_symbol` fields the self-fetch populates (last-writer-wins;
both sources read the same `CurrencyRateManager` data so they agree).

doc:
F1 wave-5 B1 — push the full instrument snapshot from Kotlin.
Writes the typed snapshot record into `state.instrument_snapshot`
so the `state()` projection observes live base/quote/tick/lot/min
instead of the default-empty values the renderer was rendering.

Also seeds `inst_id` + `trade_quote_ccy` from the snapshot when
either slot is empty so downstream consumers
(`fetch_max_available`, percent-derive, confirm payload) see a
consistent triple atomically.

Sibling parity: `spot_advanced_limit_interactor.rs::update_instrument_snapshot`
(line 3813) — the Stop sub-panel is structurally simpler so the
fan-out is narrower (no margin-mode / borrow / chevron derive).

# Wave-10 D2 USDS routing fix (2026-06-03)
User real-device (DOGE-USDⓢ pair, backend instId = "DOGE-USD"):
pre-fix Double seeded `trade_quote_ccy = snapshot.quote_ccy` which
for USDS pairs is the RAW backend value ("USD"), NOT the user-
selectable display ccy ("USDC"). Spot-limit sibling resolves the
initial value via `trade_quote_ccy_storage::
resolve_persisted_trade_quote_ccy_slice(supported_quote_ccys, ...)`
which:
1. returns the persisted user pick if it is in the new list
2. falls back to `list[0]` (the V1 display ccy) when empty
3. returns `None` when the list is empty / not USDS pair
Mirror that resolution here so MaxAvailable RPC routes
`tradeQuoteCcy=USDC` instead of leaving the param off (fallback
to "USDT" or "USD" by the backend).
Sibling Rust path:
`spot_limit_interactor.rs:1120-1138` (constructor seed) +
`:2193-2223` (InstrumentChanged handler).
